_about: Cold outreach: who to email, the email, and sending limits. See src/jobhunter/contacts.py, pitch.py, mailer.py and tracking.py. Emails are only ever sent when you click Send in `jobhunter serve`.
_small_company_max_employees: At or under this size, email the CEO/founder directly (then the CTO). Above it, the head of engineering, then HR/recruiting.
_targets: Roles in the order they are tried. Roles: ceo, founder, cto, eng_lead (head/VP/director of engineering), eng_manager, recruiter, hr.
_skip_companies: Job boards, staffing agencies and talent marketplaces: there is no hiring manager there to pitch, so these jobs show 'apply through the link'. Matched on the normalized company name.
skip_companies: IT Recruiters for Tech Jobs - itrecruiters.technology
_auto_lookup: The daily run finds contacts for that run's new shortlisted jobs, best fit first, up to the cap. Date-range runs never do (they would spend the month's credits).
_hunter_reserve_credits: Hunter lookups stop when fewer credits than this are left, so the Find contact button still works.
_claude_fallback: When Hunter knows nobody at a company, Claude (small model, 2 web searches, about $0.03-0.05) can look for the person. On click it always works; in the daily run only when this is true.
_email: Your email, word for word. {title} is the job title (noise like '- Remote' removed), {name} your name, {company} the company. The body is: Hi <first name>, / I just applied for the {title} role. <pitch_text> / <ask_text> / signature (city, phone, LinkedIn link). HR and recruiters get hr_ask_text instead of ask_text. The question asks for nothing (no call, interview or referral). pitch_mode "fixed" uses this text with no AI; "ai" lets pitch_model write the second sentence instead.
pitch_text: I led my team's move to AI-first engineering, with 115+ AI workflows running in production.
ask_text: Once this role is filled, what's the first thing you'd want that person to get right?
hr_ask_text: From your side, what quality stands out the most for this role at {company}?
_pitch: The model writing the 1-2 sentence pitch. deepseek-* models use DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (well under $0.01 per email); claude-* models use ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. The fact guard checks both the same way. Drafts are written in the daily run once a contact is known.
_follow_up_business_days: Follow-up 1 after 4 business days (Mon-Fri), follow-up 2 after 7 more. They are due in the Today view; you click to send them.
_ghost_after_business_days: No reply this long after the last follow-up was due: the job moves to Closed (ghosted). A later reply moves it back.
_caps: Emails per day (test sends to yourself do not count). Guessed addresses have their own lower cap, because bounces hurt your Gmail's reputation.
_cv: The CV attached to first emails: a PDF in cv_dir (a relative path is inside this project). A file whose name contains the company (Doe_FullStack_LigaData_Sep2026.pdf) is used for that company, else default_cv; empty means the master CV build.py makes, <Last name>_Resume_General.pdf (your name is MY_NAME in .env). You can pick another per job in the app.
_tailor: A CV tailored to one job: the model picks, orders and rewords your profile's bullets and skills for the posting; code checks every line against profile/master_profile.md and keeps your own wording where a rewrite adds anything. The layout comes from resume.md in resume_dir, and its build.py makes the PDF in cv_dir, which then becomes that job's attachment. Click Tailor CV in the app, or let the daily run do its new shortlisted jobs (best fit first, up to max_cvs_per_run). deepseek-* models use DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (about $0.01 a CV), claude-* use ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
_cv_tags: Which optional profile bullets a tailored CV prints. Each bullet in profile/master_profile.md is tagged: [core] always prints, [lead]/[fullstack]/[automation]/[mobile] only when the job matches that tag - a phrase below in its title, or in the posting (whole words, any case - except a phrase with a capital letter, which must match that case: "React" but not "react to incidents"). The same tag also picks the role's printed title (Team Lead for lead jobs). Empty means the defaults in cv.py TAG_RULES; a tag you list here replaces that tag's default lists. Example: {"lead": {"title": ["lead", "manager"], "posting": ["team lead", "mentoring"]}}
_cover: A cover letter for each job, written next to its tailored CV as cv_dir/<Last name>_CoverLetter_<Company>_<MonYYYY>.md (plain text to paste or upload). The model writes the opening, one or two paragraphs that cite your profile facts, and the closing; code checks every sentence against profile/master_profile.md (numbers, tools, titles, years) and against the word lists in cover_guidelines, and drops one that still breaks a rule after one retry. It uses only the bullets the CV prints for that job (the same tags). How letters read (length, shape, voice, words to avoid) is cover_guidelines: edit that file to change it. cover_model "claude-code" runs the Claude Code CLI (`claude -p`) signed in with your Claude account, with no tools and none of your Claude settings, CLAUDE.md or memory; "claude-code:sonnet" picks its model. Empty cover_model means cv_model. The daily run writes them for new shortlisted jobs (best fit first, up to max_covers_per_run); Write cover letter in the app or `jobhunter cover <id>` does any job.
_cover_gap_text: The sentence about what the posting asks for and your profile does not have (the model picks at most 1, and code keeps it only when the posting names it in the title or twice and your facts have nothing close; code writes this sentence, so it never claims them). {gaps} is the list, {them} is 'it' or 'them'.
cover_gap_text: I haven't worked with {gaps} yet, and I'd make learning {them} an early priority.
_catch_up_days: The daily run also tailors CVs and writes cover letters for shortlisted jobs filed this many days back that still have none (e.g. one that failed on a network error at wake-up), within the same per-run caps. 0 turns this off.
